name: Data.gov catalog (CKAN API)
description: The US federal open data catalogue - roughly half a million dataset descriptions harvested from federal, state and local publishers. Historically its CKAN API was the standard way to search all of them at once. On 2026-09-06 every documented API path returned 404; the web catalogue itself still loads. Kept here with the evidence, because a link list would still be telling you to call package_search.

license.name: US Government work; individual datasets carry their publishers' terms

access.auth_note: api.data.gov key, sent as x-api-key, for the api.gsa.gov proxy. The proxy authenticates, then 301s to catalog.data.gov, which is what is 404ing.

probes.known_broken: 404 with {"message":"Not Found"} on 2026-09-06. Also tried: /api/action/package_search, /api/3/action/site_read, /api/1/metastore/schemas/dataset/items, /api/4/harvest_sources, and the api.gsa.gov v3 proxy with a key - the proxy authenticates and then 301s straight back to this dead path. catalog.data.gov/dataset now redirects to the catalogue root.

probes.description: The api.gsa.gov v3 proxy, unauthenticated - proves the proxy is up even though the origin is not

gotchas.trap: Every tutorial, wrapper library and LLM answer about US open data starts with catalog.data.gov/api/3/action/package_search. It does not answer today.
gotchas.fix: Go to the publishing agency's own portal instead - most are CKAN or Socrata and have live APIs. See socrata-portals, and use datacite-re3data to find subject repositories.

gotchas.trap: The api.gsa.gov proxy makes the failure look like an auth problem: without a key you get a clean 403 API_KEY_MISSING, so it reads as 'I just need a key'. With a key you get a 301 to the dead origin.
gotchas.fix: Follow redirects when testing an API gateway, and check what the origin actually returns.
